sections.h2: Where deeds are recorded in Adams County
sections.html:
Head to the Adams County Courthouse, 117 Baltimore Street, Room 102, Gettysburg, where the Recorder of Deeds keeps the land records. Call 717-337-9826 between 8:00 a.m. and 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday. County holidays are closed days.

Accepting new filings ends at 4:00 p.m., thirty minutes ahead of closing time, so a package arriving at 4:20 sits until the next business day. The same counter handles realty transfer tax on behalf of the Department of Revenue, then splits the money among the state, the municipality and the school district.

Think of this office as the finish line of your sale. After you sign at closing, the deed is filed here, and the filing date is when the buyer shows up as owner in the public record.

Under the fee bill in force since December 1, 2025, one deed or mortgage is $71.25 to record, good for four pages and four names. Extras are charged on top.

Filing typeRecording fee
Deed or mortgage$71.25
Each page over 4 (deed or mortgage)$4.00
Each name over 4 (deed or mortgage)$1.00
Satisfaction piece or mortgage release$61.75
Power of attorney$18.50

Assignments of mortgage also cost $61.75, easements and rights of way $59.75, and copies $0.25 a page. A document type missing from the list gets a fee set by the Recorder. Fees are due when you record.

You may pay with cash, a check or a card; cards carry a vendor charge. Checks cannot be broken into change. If you overpay by $10 or less, the extra stays as an overpayment noted on your receipt; a larger overage means writing a new check.

Bring a checkbook. Transfer tax cannot be paid in cash and is collected as the deed is recorded. The county’s fee bill describes a 1% state tax and an equal local tax, and asks for three checks, made out to the state, to the township or borough, and to the recorder for the fee.

The buyer and seller are jointly liable. A handful of transfers are excused, among them some family transfers and property passed down by will or intestacy.

  • File a Statement of Value whenever the tax is not paid in full, and that includes a family exemption claim.
  • For land in two or more municipalities, the deed should show how the value divides so each local share is routed properly.
  • Transfers from grandparent to grandchild and between siblings appear among the recognized exemptions.
  • No deed or mortgage is recorded without a signed Certificate of Residence.

The Statement of Value is a Revenue form, and this office charges nothing to file it. For help with it, ask Revenue.

Filings have to involve real estate, show original signatures and be notarized correctly. The document date may not fall after the notary’s acknowledgment date.

Compared with neighboring counties, Adams is relaxed in a few ways. It does not use the Uniform Parcel Identifier system, which means no UPI fee, and a parcel number or street address is not required. There are no margin rules, and letter or legal paper both work.

  • Put in a stamped, self-addressed envelope. The finished document is mailed back about two weeks after it is recorded.
  • An assignment of mortgage must cite where the original mortgage is recorded, by book and page.
  • Subdivision plans are 18 by 24 inches, signed off by the municipality and the county planning commission, and recorded within 90 days of approval.
  • Remote online notarization works only during a declared emergency.

Options are a visit in person, the secure drop box by the courthouse entrance, or delivery by USPS, FedEx or UPS. An appointment is preferred though not mandatory; arrange one by phone or at registerrecorder@adamscountypa.gov.

Search terminals for the public sit in the courthouse lobby, along with a copier that works with a button from the Register and Recorder or the Prothonotary. The recording office has no terminal of its own, and taking photos of screens, books or microfilm is prohibited.

The office offers a free fraud alert called PropertyCheck, which emails or texts an owner when anything is recorded against the property. Owners who keep other land here can sign up. Also ask your title company whether the closing package can go in electronically instead of by courier.

sections.h2: The Adams County market in brief
sections.html:
Roughly 107,594 people lived here as of July 2025, a 3.6% rise since 2020. Gettysburg is the center of the county, with the national military park on three sides. Close to 78.9% of homes are occupied by their owners, and a typical owner-occupied home is valued at $268,500, which is why most local sales are owner to owner. Median household income is $84,092.

After the deed is on record, a new owner can contact the county’s Tax Services office.

Run through this list so the deed is accepted the first time.

  • A signed, notarized deed showing the notary’s venue and expiration date and a stamp you can read.
  • Three checks drawn on the right accounts, for state tax, local tax and recording fee, with amounts that match the consideration stated in the deed.
  • A completed Certificate of Residence, plus a Statement of Value if any tax is excused.
  • A stamped return envelope addressed to the buyer or the title agent.
  • Delivery before 4:00 p.m. on a weekday that is not a county holiday.

Settle ahead of time who walks the package into the courthouse and who receives the recorded original afterward.

sections.h2: How a cash sale fits in
sections.html: Paying cash leaves the recording steps alone: the deed is still signed, notarized, taxed and filed in this office. What disappears is the buyer’s lender, along with loan underwriting and the wait that comes with it. If you still owe on a mortgage, a satisfaction piece gets recorded after payoff, and its fee appears in the table above. Ask the title agent to confirm that the release is filed so the public record shows clear title.

sections.h2: A simple order of events for sellers
sections.html: Most Adams County sales run in a predictable order. The title agent prepares the deed and the tax forms, you sign before a notary, and the package goes to Room 102 with three checks. After recording, the deed is mailed back to the address on your envelope. If you are selling an inherited house, ask early which exemption, if any, applies, since a Statement of Value must accompany any claim. Sellers who live out of the area can sign with a notary near them and let the title agent handle delivery.

sections.h2: Questions to put to your title agent
sections.html: A few plain questions save a trip to Gettysburg. Who is buying the three checks and from which accounts? Does the stated price on the deed match the amount the tax is figured on? Is anyone claiming an exemption, and if so, is the Statement of Value ready? Will the agent record electronically or drive the paperwork in before the afternoon cutoff? And where should the returned original go, to you, to the buyer or to the lender? Sellers who are out of town can ask the agent to confirm each answer by email so there is a written trail. Keep the receipt from the recorder with your closing papers, since it shows the exact fees paid and the date the filing was accepted.

Once the package is accepted, nothing more is needed from you except patience. Mail return runs slow, so if the buyer or the title agent needs proof sooner, ask the agent for the stamped receipt that shows the recording date. Lenders and insurers usually accept that proof while the original travels back through the post. If a month goes by without the deed arriving, phone the recorder and give the date you filed and the names on the deed.

faqs.q: What is the base recording fee for a deed in Adams County?
faqs.a: A deed or mortgage costs $71.25 under the schedule effective December 1, 2025, plus $4.00 for each page after the fourth and $1.00 for each name after the fourth. Transfer tax is paid separately, by check.

faqs.q: When does Adams County stop accepting documents each day?
faqs.a: The cutoff is 4:00 p.m. on business days, although the office stays open until 4:30 p.m. For a special circumstance, call or email before you come.

faqs.q: Is cash accepted for transfer tax at the Adams County courthouse?
faqs.a: No. Realty transfer tax must be paid by check, with separate checks for the state tax, the local tax and the recording fee. The recording fee itself can be paid in cash or by card, with a vendor fee on cards.

faqs.q: Must a deed carry a parcel number to be recorded here?
faqs.a: No. The county does not use the UPI system, and a parcel number or property address is not required on a document. A Certificate of Residence is required, though.

faqs.q: Where should a signed deed be delivered or mailed?
faqs.a: Take it to the Recorder of Deeds at the Adams County Courthouse, 117 Baltimore Street, Room 102, Gettysburg, PA 17325, or use the drop box at the entrance. Enclose a self-addressed stamped envelope; return mail takes about two weeks.
